description_full: Taiyo Yuden Co., Ltd. develops, manufactures, and sells electronic components in Japan, North America, China, Europe, Hong Kong, Taiwan and internationally. The company provides products, such as multilayer ceramic capacitors, inductors, high frequency devices, RF devices, and aluminum electrolytic capacitors, as well as conductive polymer hybrid aluminum electrolytic capacitors. Taiyo Yuden Co., Ltd. was incorporated in 1950 and is headquartered in Tokyo, Japan.

culture_narrative: Employs approximately 20K people. Revenue per employee of $109K ranks in the bottom quartile among Technology peers. Each employee generates $18K of free cash flow annually.
financial_summary: Taiyo Yuden Co. Ltd. is a mid-cap technology business with a $5.7B market cap on $2.2B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -0% over the past three years — essentially flat, and a business treading water is rarely a path to compounding.

Returns on capital run at 2% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 22% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.

The business throws off $367M in free cash flow — roughly 16 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.93× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 1.0× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 10.8×.

Shareholder yield is only 1.2%, a thin return of capital, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.2× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
